faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: What happens if DBackup becomes unavailable - can I still restore?
faq.a1: Yes. Every backup is a standard database dump encrypted with open AES-256-GCM. With the key from your Recovery Kit and a standalone Node.js script, you can decrypt and restore without DBackup running at all.
faq.a2: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, SQLite, Redis, Valkey, Microsoft SQL Server, Azure SQL Database (beta), and Firebird (beta), with more engines added regularly.
faq.q3: Can DBackup back up files and folders, not just databases?
faq.a3: Yes. Any storage adapter can serve as a directory source - local paths, SFTP, SMB, FTP, WebDAV, S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, rsync over SSH, or Docker volumes read through the daemon. Files and databases can share one job, so the dump and the data directory that belongs to it land in the same archive and the same restore point. There is no agent to install: DBackup reads whatever those protocols reach. That agentless design is also its limit - a full run pulls the tree to the DBackup host and stages it there before packing, so it wants roughly twice the source size in free space and every byte crosses the network twice. It is built for the files that belong to the applications you already back up databases for, not for bulk media libraries; for those, restic or Borg run on the machine itself and are the better tool.
faq.q4: Can DBackup back up Docker volumes?
faq.a4: Yes, currently in beta. Pick the volumes from a list of what the Docker daemon can see, locally through its socket or on another host over SSH, and DBackup mounts them into a short-lived helper container to read them. Containers holding a selected volume are stopped for the read and started again right afterwards, per volume rather than for the whole job, and you can switch that off for data that is safe to copy live. Restoring goes back into the same volume or into a new one, though directory permissions and empty directories are not carried back yet, which is what keeps it in beta.
faq.q5: Does DBackup deduplicate like restic or Borg?
faq.a5: Not globally, and that is a deliberate trade. Incremental backups store whole changed files and reference unchanged ones in earlier archives of the same chain, so every archive stays a plain TAR you can open with tar -xf or a documented format one Node.js script reads. A chunk store would save more space but would make the backup a repository only its own tool can open - which is the lock-in DBackup exists to avoid.
faq.q6: Is there a hosted or cloud version?
faq.a6: No. DBackup is self-hosted only, distributed as a single Docker image you run on your own infrastructure.
faq.q7: What license is DBackup released under?
faq.a7: GPL-3.0. The source code is fully open and available on GitHub.
faq.q8: Can I send one backup to multiple storage destinations?
faq.a8: Yes. Multi-destination jobs upload each backup to several storage adapters at once for redundancy or off-site copies.

dbackup-agent.title: DBackup Agent
dbackup-agent.description: A small container on the target host that DBackup talks to instead of opening an SSH session, for hosts where SSH access is not an option. Dumps still stream back to DBackup for compression and encryption, so the encryption key and the storage credentials never leave it.

sync-jobs.title: Sync Jobs
sync-jobs.description: A second kind of job next to backups: keep a target in step with a source on its own schedule. Copy a file or database backup onto another host, or replicate one database into another, without building a backup and restoring it by hand every time.

stream-based-backup-pipeline.title: Stream-based Backup Pipeline
stream-based-backup-pipeline.description: Opt-in "Large DB Mode" that pipes dumps directly to storage without staging on disk first, with parallel multi-destination upload and inline checksums for databases too large for local /tmp.

runner-resilience.title: Runner Resilience
runner-resilience.description: Exponential backoff retry logic for transient errors, plus a dead letter queue for jobs that fail repeatedly and need investigation.

restic-storage-backend.title: Restic Storage Backend
restic-storage-backend.description: Restic as a storage destination with block-level deduplication and rsyncable compression, using its own repository, browsing, and retention model instead of file-based storage.

encryption-key-rotation.title: Encryption Key Rotation
encryption-key-rotation.description: Rotate the system ENCRYPTION_KEY without downtime, re-encrypting all stored secrets with the new key.

user-invite-flow.title: User Invite Flow
user-invite-flow.description: Email-based user invitations with a forced password change on first login, built on the existing SMTP notification adapter.

backup-tags-annotations.title: Backup Tags & Annotations
backup-tags-annotations.description: Manually tag backups (e.g. "pre-migration"), pin them to protect against retention deletion, and filter by tag in the Storage Explorer.

backup-anomaly-detection.title: Backup Anomaly Detection
backup-anomaly-detection.description: Alert when a backup's size deviates significantly from previous runs, plus a scheduled "test restore" task.

prometheus-metrics-endpoint.title: Prometheus Metrics Endpoint
prometheus-metrics-endpoint.description: A /metrics endpoint exposing backup count, duration, size, success rate, and queue depth, plus a ready-made Grafana dashboard.

backup-size-limits-alerts.title: Backup Size Limits & Alerts
backup-size-limits-alerts.description: Per-job configurable thresholds that warn when a backup is unexpectedly larger or smaller than expected.

backup-drift-detection.title: Backup Drift Detection
backup-drift-detection.description: Compare a database's current state against its last backup and alert when it has drifted significantly (new tables, size growth, dropped objects).

server-health-dashboard.title: Server Health Dashboard
server-health-dashboard.description: Per-adapter server health metrics (uptime, active connections, running queries, replication status) as a pre-backup health indicator.

direct-sql-execution.title: Direct SQL Execution
direct-sql-execution.description: Run custom SQL queries against configured sources from the web UI, read-only by default with write access behind a separate permission.

query-library.title: Query Library
query-library.description: Pre-built query templates for common tasks like user management and table maintenance, available as quick actions in the UI.

user-privileges-viewer.title: User & Privileges Viewer
user-privileges-viewer.description: Read-only view of database users and their permissions, to verify the backup user has sufficient privileges as a security audit helper.

storage-trend-graph.title: Storage Trend Graph
storage-trend-graph.description: Historical database size over time derived from backup metadata, with growth-rate visualization for capacity planning.

e2e-test-suite.title: End-to-End Test Suite
e2e-test-suite.description: Playwright/Cypress coverage for critical flows - login, create job, run backup, restore, verify - running in CI.

internationalization.title: Internationalization (i18n)
internationalization.description: Multi-language UI support with room for community-contributed translations.

high-contrast-mode.title: High-Contrast Mode
high-contrast-mode.description: A high-contrast theme next to light and dark, for better readability and accessibility.

oracle-support.title: Oracle Support
oracle-support.description: Oracle Database as a new supported source, using RMAN or Data Pump exports.

influxdb-support.title: InfluxDB Support
influxdb-support.description: InfluxDB as a new supported source for backing up time-series data.

redesigned-interface.title: Redesigned Interface
redesigned-interface.description: Every page is rebuilt in a new design that also works on phones and tablets, with a search across all jobs, connections, backups and runs. New pages for the backups, the databases and the history of each run, a Quick Setup that adds the first backup in one place, and notification emails in the same look.

single-database-restores-downloads.title: Single Database Restores & Downloads
single-database-restores-downloads.description: Restore or download one database out of a multi-database backup, reading only that database from the destination. Old execution logs and history entries can be cleaned up automatically, and Settings shows and optimizes the size of the DBackup database.

300-github-stars.title: 300 GitHub Stars
300-github-stars.description: DBackup crossed 300 stars on GitHub, thanks to everyone in the community.

azure-sql-database-support.title: Azure SQL Database Support
azure-sql-database-support.description: Azure SQL Database as a new source in beta, backed up through a BACPAC export, plus an hourly tier for Smart (GFS) retention policies.

docker-volume-backups.title: Docker Volume Backups
docker-volume-backups.description: Docker volumes as a backup source (beta), listed from the target host the way databases already are, so you pick them instead of typing paths. Containers using a selected volume are stopped for the export and started again afterwards, which you can turn off per source when the data is safe to copy live.

file-folder-backups.title: File & Folder Backups
file-folder-backups.description: Directory and file sources with a seekable, per-entry encrypted archive format, incremental backup chains, byte-range restores, and a completely rebuilt Recovery Kit.

200-github-stars.title: 200 GitHub Stars
200-github-stars.description: DBackup crossed 200 stars on GitHub, thanks to everyone in the community.

firebird-support.title: Firebird Support
firebird-support.description: Firebird (3.x/4.x/5.x) as a supported database source, with direct and SSH connection modes.

valkey-support.title: Valkey Database Support
valkey-support.description: Valkey as a database source, using the same RDB backup mechanism as Redis.

notification-templates.title: Notification Templates
notification-templates.description: Reusable, per-channel, event-filtered notification templates replacing flat per-job notification config.

backup-integrity-verification.title: Backup Integrity Verification
backup-integrity-verification.description: SHA-256/MD5 checksums, on-demand Verify Now, native checksum verification across adapters, and scheduled integrity checks.

vault-credential-profiles-extended.title: Vault Credential Profiles for Webhooks & OAuth
vault-credential-profiles-extended.description: Credential vault profiles extended to WEBHOOK, OAUTH, and TOKEN types.

database-explorer-version-history.title: Database Explorer Version History
database-explorer-version-history.description: An engine-version timeline and change log per database source.

database-explorer-drill-down.title: Database Explorer
database-explorer-drill-down.description: A table/data viewer with pagination, search, and schema inspection across all adapters.

templates-system.title: Templates System
templates-system.description: A dedicated Templates page with reusable Retention Policies, Naming Templates, and Schedule Presets, assignable across jobs.

credential-profile-system.title: Credential Profile System
credential-profile-system.description: Centralized, encrypted Credential Profiles that adapters reference instead of storing secrets inline, plus one-click cloning for sources, destinations, and jobs.

live-history-redesign.title: Live History Redesign
live-history-redesign.description: Pipeline-stage tracking with real-time speed and progress for every backup and restore.

ssh-remote-execution.title: SSH Remote Execution
ssh-remote-execution.description: Run backups directly on the remote database host via SSH, without a local database client.

https-by-default.title: HTTPS by Default & Certificate Management
https-by-default.description: Built-in HTTPS with auto-generated certificates by default, plus a Certificate Management UI.

first-stable-release.title: First Stable Release
first-stable-release.description: The first stable release, stabilizing the platform after the beta phase.

500-github-stars.title: 500 GitHub Stars
500-github-stars.description: Help DBackup reach its next community milestone.
